 Judgment

In this appeal filed under Section 383 Cr.P.C., the appellant, the sole accused, in S.C.No.828/2017 on the file of the Court of the Special Judge for the Trial of offences against Women and Children,
Thalassery, challenges the conviction entered and sentence passed against him for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 Part I IPC.

2. The prosecution case is that on a day about 9 months before 09/03/2017 at about 02:30 p.m.,
while PW1 was walking towards her house through Thurumbi road, the accused followed her, caught hold of her and dragged her to a nearby forest area and committed rape on her.
The accused on three successive days thereafter also committed rape on PW1 at the very same place.
The accused threatened PW1 with dire 2025:KER:19805 consequences in case she dared to reveal the incident to others.

Hence as per the final report/charge sheet, the accused is alleged have to committed the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)
(n) and 506 Part I IPC.
3.

The final report/charge sheet was filed before the jurisdictional magistrate, who after complying with all the necessary formalities contemplated under Section 209 Cr.P.C., committed the case to the Court of Session, Thalassery.
The case was taken on file and made over to the Court of the Special Judge/Additional Sessions Judge-I, Thalassery for trial and disposal.

sentences.text: 4. On appearance of the accused before the trial court, a charge under Section 376(2)(n) and 506 Part I IPC was framed, read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty.
5. On behalf of the prosecution, PW1 to PW12 were examined and Exts.P1 to P9 were marked.

After the close of the prosecution evidence, the accused was questioned under 2025:KER:19805 Section 313(1)(b) Cr.P.C. with regard to the incriminating circumstances appearing against him in the evidence of the prosecution.
The accused denied all those circumstances and maintained his innocence.
6. As the trial court did not find it a fit case to acquit the accused under Section 232 Cr.P.C., he was asked to enter on his defence and adduce evidence in support thereof.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the accused.

Ext.D1 is the contradiction brought out in the testimony of PW4.
7.

On consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, the trial court by the impugned judgment found the accused guilty of the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) and 506 Part I IPC.

Hence the accused has been sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for Suresh.E.K vs State Of Kerala on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155797371/
2 14 years and to fine of 1,00,000/- and in default to rigorous imprisonment for one year and to rigorous imprisonment for one year for the offence punishable under Section 506 Part I IPC.
The substantive sentences have been directed to run concurrently and the default 2025:KER:19805 sentences, consecutively.
Set off under Section 428 Cr.P.C. has been allowed.
The fine amount, if realised, has been directed to be paid as compensation under Section 357(1)(b) Cr.P.C. to PW1.
Aggrieved, the accused has come up in appeal.
8. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether the conviction entered and sentence passed against the appellant/accused by the trial court are sustainable or not.

9. Heard both sides.
10.

It was submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant/accused that the testimony of PW1 would make it clear that she has no complaints against the accused and that Ext.P1 FIS was given at the instance of her brother and family.
The ingredients of the offence under Section 375 IPC is not made out and therefore the trial court went wrong in convicting the accused, goes the arguments.

Per contra, it was submitted by the learned public prosecutor that PW1 has mild intellectual disability, that is, disability about 50% and therefore she was not sure as to what she 2025:KER:19805 was saying.
A reading of her deposition would show that she had not consented to the coitus and that it was infact a case of rape.
There are no infirmities in the impugned judgment calling for an interference by this Court, argued the learned public prosecutor.
11. I briefly refer to the evidence relied on by the prosecution in support of the case.
PW1 deposed that during the time of the incident she was residing with her brother, her sister- in-law and nephew.
She used to do all the household chores as well as go to the milk booth to deliver milk.
On the date of the incident at about 02:45 p.m. while she was returning home after delivering milk, the accused caught hold of her, dragged her into the nearby bushes and raped her.
The accused repeated the said act on two other days also.
He threatened her with dire consequences if she revealed the incident to others.
During the early morning hours of 09/03/2017, she had stomach pain.
She went to the toilet where she gave birth to a child.
She was attended by her sister-in-law.
When her sister-in-law enquired about the matter, she disclosed that it was the accused who was 2025:KER:19805 responsible for her pregnancy.
Her brother gave a complaint to the police.
She admitted giving Ext.P1 FIS to the police on 09/03/2017.
11.1. PW2, sister-in-law of PW1 deposed that the latter has mild intellectual disability.
On 09/03/2017 at 03:00 a.m., PW1 gave birth to a child in the toilet of their house.
She came to know about the same on hearing the cries of the child from the toilet.
When PW2 questioned PW1 regarding the paternity of the child, the latter told the name of the accused.
PW1 disclosed that the accused had raped her by taking her into the bushes situated near their house and that the act was repeated on two subsequent occasions also.
11.2. PW3, the son of PW2 and nephew of PW1, deposed in tune with the testimony of PW2.
PW3 also has a case that PW1 has mild intellectual disability issues.
Suresh.

3 11.3.
PW6, Consultant, Gynecology, Taluk Hospital, Taliparamba, deposed that on 09/03/2017 she had examined PW1 and issued Ext.P3 certificate.
The history was narrated as rape by 2025:KER:19805 Sureshkumar (the accused).
Her examination suggested recent vaginal delivery.
12. The prosecution neither in the FIR nor in the final report has a case that PW1 has mild intellectual disability and that her disability is 50%.
This is a new case that is seen brought in by PW2 and PW3 in the box.
According to PW2, there are also records/certificate to show that PW1 has 50% disability.

However, for reasons best known to the prosecution, the said record has not been produced before the court and hence there is no material(s) before the court to find that PW1 was in any way intellectually disabled.

On going through the impugned judgment, I find that the prosecution never had a case during the course of the trial or any time before or after that PW1 was not a competent witness due to her alleged intellectual disability.
On going through the testimony of PW1, I find that she has given quite rational answers during her examination and hence she was certainly a competent witness.
13. PW1 in her chief examination fully supported 2025:KER:19805 the prosecution case.

However,
in the cross-examination, she deposed that she has no complaints against the accused and that it is her brother and PW2 his wife who have complaints against the accused.
Apart from the testimony of PW1, the other prosecution witnesses have only hearsay knowledge about the incident.

It is true that the sole testimony of the prosecutrix alone is sufficient to arrive at the guilt of the accused, provided the testimony of the prosecutrix is credible and inspires confidence in the mind of the court.
In such circumstances, the testimony of the prosecutrix should be of sterling quality.
PW1 admittedly was a major at the time of the incident.
Even going by the prosecution case, the accused is alleged to have raped PW1 on three occassions and all these acts were committed at the same place on three different days.
The incident is alleged to have happened about 9 months before 09/03/2017.
The FIS was 2025:KER:19805 given only after she delivered a child.
PW1 has a case that the accused had threatened her with dire consequences and hence the reason why she did not disclose the incident to others.

But, as noticed earlier, her case in the cross examination is that she had no complaints against the accused and that it was at the instance of her brother and family she had given the complaint to the police.
That appears to be the reason why no complaint was given to the police immediately after the incident, though the accused is alleged to have repeated the abuse on two other subsequent occasions also.
From the materials on record, I do not find any reason to disbelieve the version of PW1 that due to the sexual encounters with the accused she had conceived and delivered a child.
But that would not make out an offence under Section 375 IPC.
Her only grievance seems to be that the accused is not maintaining the child.
The testimony of PW1 raises doubts as to whether the sexual encounters which took place were infact without her consent.
That being the position, I find that the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the conviction and sentence imposed against the appellant by the trial court for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 Part I IPC is set aside.
The accused is acquitted under Section 235(1) Cr.P.C.

He is set at liberty and his bail bond shall stand cancelled.
Suresh.
